title: Verify element text editing functions correctly in Visual Editor under valid conditions
preconditions: User has an active VWO account with edit access to a live project configured for Visual Editor.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Visual Editor and open the configuration for element text editing.
3. Enter valid, supported values for element text editing.
4. Save the configuration and publish/activate it.
5. Trigger the scenario on the target page or app and observe the behavior.
expected: Element text editing behaves exactly as configured, with no errors logged in the browser console or VWO dashboard, and the change is reflected in real time.

title: Verify Visual Editor handles invalid input gracefully for element text editing
preconditions: User has edit access to Visual Editor with element text editing available to configure.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Visual Editor and open the configuration for element text editing.
3. Submit invalid or malformed values for element text editing (empty required fields, out-of-range numbers, unsupported characters).
4. Attempt to save the configuration.
expected: The system rejects the invalid input with a clear inline validation message, does not persist a broken configuration, and does not throw an unhandled exception.

title: Verify element text editing at minimum and maximum allowed limits in Visual Editor
preconditions: Documented min/max limits for element text editing are available from product spec.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Visual Editor and locate the element text editing setting.
3. Set the value to the documented minimum allowed limit and save.
4. Repeat with the documented maximum allowed limit.
5. Attempt one unit beyond each limit.
expected: Values at the minimum and maximum limits are accepted and applied correctly; values beyond the limits are rejected with an appropriate error message.

title: Verify element text editing in Visual Editor is not vulnerable to injection or unauthorized access
preconditions: Tester has both a low-privilege account and API tooling (e.g. Postman/curl).
steps:
1. Log in with a low-privilege user account.
2. Attempt to access or modify element text editing directly via API/URL manipulation without the required role.
3. Submit script tags, SQL-like payloads, and oversized payloads into element text editing input fields.
4. Inspect network requests for sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, PII).
expected: Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with a 401/403 response, injected payloads are sanitized/escaped and never executed or persisted verbatim, and no sensitive data is exposed in responses.

title: Verify element text editing in Visual Editor performs within acceptable thresholds under load
preconditions: Load-testing tool (e.g. k6/JMeter) is available and pointed at a staging project.
steps:
1. Configure element text editing with a realistic production-scale dataset (e.g. high-traffic campaign or large audience segment).
2. Measure page/API response time for the associated action.
3. Repeat the measurement under concurrent load (e.g. 100 simulated concurrent users).
expected: Element text editing completes within the agreed SLA (e.g. under 200ms for API calls, under 2s for page render), with no memory leaks or degraded performance under sustained load.

title: Verify element text editing in Visual Editor is intuitive and provides clear guidance
preconditions: Tester has no prior training on this feature and is given only the task, not the docs.
steps:
1. Open the configuration screen for element text editing as a first-time user.
2. Attempt to complete the primary task without consulting external documentation.
3. Note any confusing labels, missing tooltips, or unclear error states.
expected: A new user can complete the element text editing task without external help; tooltips or help text are present for non-obvious fields, and error states clearly explain the corrective action.

title: Regression check: element text editing in Visual Editor continues to work after the latest release
preconditions: A last-known-good baseline (screenshot/recording) exists for this scenario.

2. Compare the observed behavior against the last known-good baseline.

expected: Element text editing behaves identically to the last known-good baseline; no previously fixed defects have resurfaced.

3. Perform one critical happy-path action end to end.

steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Visual Editor and open the configuration for custom JavaScript injection.
3. Submit invalid or malformed values for custom JavaScript injection (empty required fields, out-of-range numbers, unsupported characters).
4. Attempt to save the configuration.
expected: The system rejects the invalid input with a clear inline validation message, does not persist a broken configuration, and does not throw an unhandled exception.

title: Verify custom JavaScript injection at minimum and maximum allowed limits in Visual Editor
preconditions: Documented min/max limits for custom JavaScript injection are available from product spec.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Visual Editor and locate the custom JavaScript injection setting.
3. Set the value to the documented minimum allowed limit and save.
4. Repeat with the documented maximum allowed limit.
5. Attempt one unit beyond each limit.
expected: Values at the minimum and maximum limits are accepted and applied correctly; values beyond the limits are rejected with an appropriate error message.

title: Verify custom JavaScript injection in Visual Editor is not vulnerable to injection or unauthorized access
preconditions: Tester has both a low-privilege account and API tooling (e.g. Postman/curl).
steps:
1. Log in with a low-privilege user account.
2. Attempt to access or modify custom JavaScript injection directly via API/URL manipulation without the required role.
3. Submit script tags, SQL-like payloads, and oversized payloads into custom JavaScript injection input fields.
4. Inspect network requests for sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, PII).
expected: Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with a 401/403 response, injected payloads are sanitized/escaped and never executed or persisted verbatim, and no sensitive data is exposed in responses.

title: Verify custom JavaScript injection in Visual Editor performs within acceptable thresholds under load
preconditions: Load-testing tool (e.g. k6/JMeter) is available and pointed at a staging project.
steps:
1. Configure custom JavaScript injection with a realistic production-scale dataset (e.g. high-traffic campaign or large audience segment).
2. Measure page/API response time for the associated action.
3. Repeat the measurement under concurrent load (e.g. 100 simulated concurrent users).
expected: Custom JavaScript injection completes within the agreed SLA (e.g. under 200ms for API calls, under 2s for page render), with no memory leaks or degraded performance under sustained load.

title: Verify custom JavaScript injection in Visual Editor is intuitive and provides clear guidance
preconditions: Tester has no prior training on this feature and is given only the task, not the docs.
steps:
1. Open the configuration screen for custom JavaScript injection as a first-time user.
2. Attempt to complete the primary task without consulting external documentation.
3. Note any confusing labels, missing tooltips, or unclear error states.
expected: A new user can complete the custom JavaScript injection task without external help; tooltips or help text are present for non-obvious fields, and error states clearly explain the corrective action.

title: Regression check: custom JavaScript injection in Visual Editor continues to work after the latest release
preconditions: A last-known-good baseline (screenshot/recording) exists for this scenario.

2. Compare the observed behavior against the last known-good baseline.

steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Audience Targeting and Segmentation and open the configuration for UTM parameter targeting.
3. Enter valid, supported values for UTM parameter targeting.
4. Save the configuration and publish/activate it.
5. Trigger the scenario on the target page or app and observe the behavior.
expected: UTM parameter targeting behaves exactly as configured, with no errors logged in the browser console or VWO dashboard, and the change is reflected in real time.

title: Verify Audience Targeting and Segmentation handles invalid input gracefully for UTM parameter targeting
preconditions: User has edit access to Audience Targeting and Segmentation with UTM parameter targeting available to configure.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Audience Targeting and Segmentation and open the configuration for UTM parameter targeting.
3. Submit invalid or malformed values for UTM parameter targeting (empty required fields, out-of-range numbers, unsupported characters).
4. Attempt to save the configuration.
expected: The system rejects the invalid input with a clear inline validation message, does not persist a broken configuration, and does not throw an unhandled exception.

title: Verify UTM parameter targeting at minimum and maximum allowed limits in Audience Targeting and Segmentation
preconditions: Documented min/max limits for UTM parameter targeting are available from product spec.
steps:
1. Log in to the VWO dashboard with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Audience Targeting and Segmentation and locate the UTM parameter targeting setting.
3. Set the value to the documented minimum allowed limit and save.
4. Repeat with the documented maximum allowed limit.
5. Attempt one unit beyond each limit.
expected: Values at the minimum and maximum limits are accepted and applied correctly; values beyond the limits are rejected with an appropriate error message.

title: Verify UTM parameter targeting in Audience Targeting and Segmentation is not vulnerable to injection or unauthorized access
preconditions: Tester has both a low-privilege account and API tooling (e.g. Postman/curl).
steps:
1. Log in with a low-privilege user account.
2. Attempt to access or modify UTM parameter targeting directly via API/URL manipulation without the required role.
3. Submit script tags, SQL-like payloads, and oversized payloads into UTM parameter targeting input fields.
4. Inspect network requests for sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, PII).
expected: Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with a 401/403 response, injected payloads are sanitized/escaped and never executed or persisted verbatim, and no sensitive data is exposed in responses.

title: Verify UTM parameter targeting in Audience Targeting and Segmentation performs within acceptable thresholds under load
preconditions: Load-testing tool (e.g. k6/JMeter) is available and pointed at a staging project.
steps:
1. Configure UTM parameter targeting with a realistic production-scale dataset (e.g. high-traffic campaign or large audience segment).
2. Measure page/API response time for the associated action.
3. Repeat the measurement under concurrent load (e.g. 100 simulated concurrent users).
expected: UTM parameter targeting completes within the agreed SLA (e.g. under 200ms for API calls, under 2s for page render), with no memory leaks or degraded performance under sustained load.

title: Verify UTM parameter targeting in Audience Targeting and Segmentation is intuitive and provides clear guidance
preconditions: Tester has no prior training on this feature and is given only the task, not the docs.
steps:

2. Attempt to complete the primary task without consulting external documentation.
3. Note any confusing labels, missing tooltips, or unclear error states.
expected: A new user can complete the UTM parameter targeting task without external help; tooltips or help text are present for non-obvious fields, and error states clearly explain the corrective action.

title: Verify notification AB variant delivery in Push Notifications is not vulnerable to injection or unauthorized access - Safari (iOS 18)
preconditions: Tester has both a low-privilege account and API tooling (e.g. Postman/curl). Test environment/context: Safari (iOS 18).
steps:
1. Log in with a low-privilege user account.
2. Attempt to access or modify notification AB variant delivery directly via API/URL manipulation without the required role.
3. Submit script tags, SQL-like payloads, and oversized payloads into notification AB variant delivery input fields.
4. Inspect network requests for sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, PII).

expected: Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with a 401/403 response, injected payloads are sanitized/escaped and never executed or persisted verbatim, and no sensitive data is exposed in responses.

title: Verify drag-and-drop reorder in Visual Editor is not vulnerable to injection or unauthorized access - Chrome (Desktop, Windows 11)
preconditions: Tester has both a low-privilege account and API tooling (e.g. Postman/curl). Test environment/context: Chrome (Desktop, Windows 11).
steps:
1. Log in with a low-privilege user account.
2. Attempt to access or modify drag-and-drop reorder directly via API/URL manipulation without the required role.
3. Submit script tags, SQL-like payloads, and oversized payloads into drag-and-drop reorder input fields.
4. Inspect network requests for sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, PII).
5. Repeat the scenario specifically on: Chrome (Desktop, Windows 11).
expected: Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with a 401/403 response, injected payloads are sanitized/escaped and never executed or persisted verbatim, and no sensitive data is exposed in responses.
